intro: Tuesday June 24. Two events since the June 23 long-term update have altered the structural conviction calibration across the watchlist — one upgrade and one downgrade. UPGRADE: SpaceX (SPCX) long-term conviction upgraded from MEDIUM to HIGH on the $89B bond demand confirmation ($20B offering, 4.4x oversubscribed) — the most powerful institutional franchise validation since the Moody's Baa1 / S&P BBB / Fitch BBB+ ratings, and categorically more powerful because it reflects $89B of private capital putting real money on SpaceX credit quality. DOWNGRADE: Bitcoin (BTC-USD) long-term conviction downgraded from MEDIUM to LOW on Day 2 stop execution ($62,377 confirmed at 11:07 UTC, full exit gate triggered per the two-consecutive-UTC-daily-close protocol) — the fixed-supply × ETF-access × halving thesis remains structurally intact but requires re-entry confirmation after macro regime normalizes. No changes to NVDA (HIGH), MSFT (HIGH), SK Hynix (MEDIUM), GOOGL (MEDIUM), AMZN (MEDIUM). New near-term risk added to GOOGL: AI talent exodus (Noam Shazeer to OpenAI, Gabriel Jumper to Anthropic) confirmed in June 23 media; management has not announced a retention program; this is a moat-discount session for GOOGL until a senior AI retention announcement is made. Long-term GOOGL thesis unchanged (TPU inference cost advantage, Gemini frontier model leadership, search moat resilience) but near-term confidence requires Q2 earnings (mid-July) to demonstrate AI Overviews monetization progress. The June 24 compound catalyst (NVDA Annual Meeting + Micron Q3) is the conviction reset event for all AI names in this list — a Micron beat-and-raise on HBM demand (revenue $34.66B+, Q4 guidance $36B+, HBM sold-out through 2027) is the single most important structural data point of H1 2026 for every long-term AI thesis here.

ideas.name: NVIDIA
ideas.idea: Annual Meeting override active today (June 24, 9 AM PT) — Jensen Huang's first post-FOMC public AI demand commentary; KOSPI +3.26% removes Korea-panic overhang; $200 floor held through Black Tuesday; Micron Q3 tonight is the HBM supply chain validation; structural accumulation window at $200–$215.
ideas.why: NVDA's fundamental thesis has strengthened through the June 23 macro stress: the Annual Meeting override rule was specifically designed for the scenario now in force (DXY gate failed + Annual Meeting date arriving), and today is the delivery date for that override. The June 23 SOXX -7.88% / NVDA -3.09% selloff at 24M volume (16% of 30-day average) was the clearest 'forced institutional liquidation' signal in the 2026 cycle — the kind of anomalous-volume, macro-driven de-rating that long-term accumulation frameworks are designed to exploit. NVDA at $200–$208 is approximately 30x forward FY27 earnings (~$91B revenue consensus) — the most compelling entry since early 2026. The June 24 compound event (Jensen Annual Meeting 9 AM PT + Micron Q3 HBM confirmation after close) is the framework's near-term catalyst pair before the thesis runs to August earnings. The $200 floor held overnight, KOSPI +3.26% removes the Korea-triggered AI chip panic overhang, and NVDA premarket +1.6% confirms institutional buyers are positioning ahead of the Annual Meeting.
ideas.driver: Hyperscaler + sovereign AI capex compounding through 2028+ (Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, xAI all committed through at least 2027); Vera Rubin rack-scale systems entering production 2026–2027 with HBM4E supply chain locked; CUDA ecosystem moat expanding into robotics and physical AI (Project GR00T, NeMo platform); 62-analyst consensus PT ~$299 = +43% from ~$209; inference demand following training ramp creates durable second wave; Annual Meeting June 24 is the conviction reset event for the AI capex cycle.
ideas.risk: Custom ASICs (Google TPU v6, AWS Trainium 3, Meta MTIA 2) erode H100/B200 inference share faster than expected over 2027–2028; Micron Q3 miss on HBM revenue signals AI memory demand cycle peaking before Vera Rubin ramp completes; sustained 30Y above 5.25% structurally compresses AI-capex multiples across the sector; May PCE June 25 hot print triggers multi-week risk-off that extends the macro-gate failures.

ideas.name: SK Hynix (000660.KS)
ideas.idea: KOSPI +3.26% recovery validates June 23 was panic-driven, not structural; estimated close ₩2,638,000; framework stop ₩2,540,000 not triggered; Micron Q3 tonight is the direct HBM demand read-through; ADR SEC clearance imminent (late June); conviction remains MEDIUM until Micron Q3 confirms HBM sold-out status.
ideas.why: The June 24 KOSPI recovery (+3.26%) is the primary evidence that the June 23 ATH reversal (-12.47%) was driven by macro forces (BofA 3-hike note, leveraged KOSPI position unwinds, Broadcom guidance miss) rather than SK Hynix-specific fundamentals. The framework stop (₩2,540,000) was never triggered on a daily closing basis — the two-consecutive-close rule held. The structural thesis remains intact: 58% global HBM market share, HBM4E 12-layer confirmed shipments (June 18), NVIDIA supply lock through 2030, ADR Nasdaq listing imminent ($14B raise + $66B total shareholder return program). Conviction remains MEDIUM (not HIGH) because: (1) HBM4 capacity slowdown report (Korean media June 23) requires management rebuttal; (2) Cheongju plant accident requires quantified assessment; (3) Samsung HBM4E competition requires Micron Q3 data to dismiss. Tonight's Micron Q3 is the near-term inflection — a beat-and-raise upgrades long-term conviction to HIGH and drives sell-side PT revisions above ₩2,900,000.
ideas.driver: HBM4→4E product transition with SK Hynix as performance leader (58% share, 12-layer confirmed, shortage through 2028); NVIDIA supply lock through 2030; ADR Nasdaq listing July–August 2026 creating structural US passive fund demand channel ($66B total return including $14B ADR raise + ₩75T+ buyback); mandatory sell-side PT revision cascade from ₩2,690,000 to ₩3.0M+ once Micron Q3 confirms HBM demand; KOSPI 9,000 passive inflow structural bid.
ideas.risk: Samsung executes credible HBM4E capacity ramp with specific NVIDIA qualification announcement before SK Hynix completes qualification (raised by June 23 competition reports); ADR SEC clearance delayed materially beyond June (removes near-term demand catalyst); Micron Q3 HBM miss with Q4 downward guidance directly de-rates SK Hynix on June 25 KST; SK Hynix management officially confirms HBM4 capacity slowdown at any public forum.

ideas.name: Microsoft
ideas.idea: Lowest-risk path to enterprise AI monetization — the most rate-insensitive megacap with contracted Azure AI workloads; June 23 macro-driven dip to ~$370–$375 est. is the structural accumulation window; Micron Q3 HBM sold-out confirmation directly validates Azure AI workload growth expectations.
ideas.why: Microsoft's enterprise AI thesis is the most rate-insensitive in the megacap cohort: contracted enterprise Azure bookings at fixed prices for 12–36 months mean Microsoft's near-term revenue is not directly affected by VIX spikes, DXY moves, or SPX selloffs. The June 23 macro stress that challenged BTC (fixed supply in risk-off), SK Hynix (equity volatility circuit breakers), and NVDA (AI capex multiple compression) does not touch MSFT's contracted enterprise subscription cash flows. Micron Q3 sold-out HBM through 2027 is directly positive for Azure AI workload growth expectations — Azure is one of the primary HBM customers via its Maia 100 accelerator program and third-party NVIDIA workloads. The Copilot enterprise adoption is compounding across hundreds of millions of seats with pricing power increasing as capabilities improve. At ~$370–$375 post-FOMC, MSFT is the safest vehicle for 3–5 year AI exposure with the lowest framework gate complexity.
ideas.driver: Azure AI workload attach rates compounding; Copilot enterprise adoption across hundreds of millions of seats at increasing pricing tiers ($30/mo Copilot for Microsoft 365 compound); OpenAI relationship providing frontier model differentiation and enterprise AI bundle pricing power; subscription model providing rate-insensitive contracted cash flows; Teams + Dynamics + Power Platform AI integration creating switching-cost reinforced moats.
ideas.risk: AI capex-to-Azure-revenue monetization lag extends beyond H2 2026 (revenue growth deceleration signals); antitrust scrutiny of OpenAI relationship limits bundling opportunities in EU/UK; SPCX Cursor AI (1M+ developers) displaces GitHub Copilot over 2–4 years via AI-native developer tooling category creation; cloud spending deceleration if BofA 3-hike 2026 forecast materializes into enterprise IT budget tightening.

ideas.name: Alphabet
ideas.idea: Long-term thesis unchanged — cheapest full-stack AI at the megacap lowest forward multiple; NEW NEAR-TERM RISK: AI talent exodus (Noam Shazeer to OpenAI, Gabriel Jumper to Anthropic) is a moat-discount narrative that requires management retention response; short/puts on bounces to $355–$370 are the near-term expression; Q2 mid-July is the first structural positive catalyst.
ideas.why: Alphabet's fundamental long-term thesis is unchanged: Gemini frontier models, TPU inference cost leadership (30–40% cost advantage over NVIDIA GPU workloads at scale), Search generating the cash to fund everything, YouTube as the second-largest advertising surface. At ~$341.50 (cumulative -16.5% over two sessions), GOOGL's forward multiple is the lowest in the megacap cohort. However, the June 23 AI talent exodus reports (Noam Shazeer to OpenAI, Gabriel Jumper to Anthropic) represent a new qualitative risk that the previous high-conviction framework did not price: Google's AI research moat depends on retaining the researchers who built it. Each session without a Google counter-narrative (retention program, equity compensation restructuring, named executive commitment) is a moat-discount session. The long-term conviction remains MEDIUM — the TPU/Gemini/Search structural advantages are durable and the talent exodus may be a short-term narrative rather than a structural shift. Q2 mid-July earnings is the first catalyst that demonstrates whether AI Overviews monetization is progressing as expected.
ideas.driver: TPU-driven inference cost advantage creating Google Cloud AI pricing power vs Azure and AWS; Gemini integration across billion-user surfaces (Search, YouTube, Gmail, Maps, Android); Google Cloud AI workload attach rates inflecting upward; potential search-moat expansion rather than AI cannibalization (Q1 2026 session-length data); international advertising revenue benefiting structurally from eventual DXY decline; Android and Play Store ecosystem providing AI distribution moat.
ideas.risk: AI talent exodus (Shazeer/Jumper departures) accelerates without senior management retention response — if three additional top AI researchers leave before Q2 earnings, the moat-discount narrative becomes a thesis-level concern; DOJ antitrust remedies fracture the search + advertising bundle (regulatory separation risk unique to GOOGL); AI Overviews prove to be session-length headwind in Q2 2026 data (reversing Q1 thesis); higher-for-longer rates (BofA 3-hike 2026) extend multiple compression before AI Overviews thesis compounds.

ideas.name: SpaceX
ideas.idea: LONG-TERM CONVICTION UPGRADED TO HIGH on $89B bond demand — 4.4x oversubscribed confirms IG quality is not in doubt; near-term step-aside framework unchanged (bond distribution + below $185 gate); September 2 first earnings is the structural re-entry catalyst with $89B demand as the balance sheet confidence anchor.
ideas.why: The $89B in institutional fixed-income demand for SpaceX's $20B bond offering is the most important franchise validation since the Moody's Baa1 / S&P BBB / Fitch BBB+ ratings. It upgrades the long-term thesis from 'franchise quality implied by IG ratings' to 'franchise quality confirmed by $89B of institutional capital willing to lend money at IG rates.' Institutional fixed-income investors (pension funds, insurance companies, sovereign wealth funds) who submitted $89B in orders independently underwrite credit quality — they are not making sentiment-driven decisions. The $89B demand places SpaceX in the top tier of IG debut borrowers and validates the franchise economics that underpin the equity thesis. Long-term conviction is HIGH because: (1) $89B demand = balance sheet credibility for the 3–5 year horizon; (2) Starlink $20B+ annualized revenue trajectory; (3) Starship 10–50x cost-to-orbit economics creating a new satellite economy; (4) Cursor AI ($60B acquisition, 1M+ developers, not in any IG rating model) as a software revenue layer call option at effectively zero additional equity cost; (5) Starshield national security base load; (6) September 2 first earnings with this $89B confirmation is a more powerful setup than September 2 would have been without it. Near-term step-aside is unchanged: two consecutive closes above $185 remain required; bond distribution clears ~July 1–6; $150 defense line is the monitoring floor.
ideas.driver: ★ $89B bond demand (June 24) — 4.4x oversubscribed institutional validation of IG credit quality at unprecedented scale; Starlink subscriber and ARPU compounding toward $20B+ annualized revenue (5M+ subs, ~$120/month); Starship cost-to-orbit economics enabling new satellite economy (10–50x cost reduction); Cursor AI software revenue layer (1M+ developers, not in IG rating models, $60B acquisition); Starshield national-security revenue base providing government contract stability; IG ratings permanently lowering cost of capital to investment-grade spreads; September 2 first earnings = public financial disclosure initiating institutional equity coverage.
ideas.risk: IPO-cycle overvaluation requires sustained multiple compression before value investors engage (80x revenue at $156 is still an extreme US public equity valuation multiple); September 2 first earnings disappoints vs $2.14T implied market cap expectations — if Starlink growth is below 35% YoY or Cursor AI revenue is immaterial, the $160 entry does not look cheap; key-person concentration risk (Elon Musk political exposure — any major political controversy creates equity multiple compression); December 9 lock-up expiry first major supply event — float expansion from ~4% to 9–14% creates structural selling ceiling.

ideas.name: Amazon
ideas.idea: AWS AI infrastructure + Hormuz logistics tailwind — post-FOMC + Black Tuesday dip to ~$175–$180 est. is the best megacap cloud entry; Micron Q3 June 24 is the direct AWS AI workload validation event; subscription model insulates against VIX/DXY macro stress.
ideas.why: Amazon runs the world's largest commercial cloud (AWS), is ramping Trainium/Inferentia custom silicon to reduce AI inference costs, and operates the logistics-Prime flywheel that scales into robotic AI fulfillment. Micron Q3 confirmation of sold-out HBM through 2027 directly validates AWS AI workload growth through 2027 — AWS is a primary HBM customer via its Ultracluster AI infrastructure. The Iran ceasefire Hormuz logistics tailwind is Amazon-specific: shipping cost normalization as Hormuz commercial traffic returns reduces Prime delivery margins and fulfillment center costs by an estimated 5–10%. The June 23 macro selloff adds to the post-FOMC discount on AMZN — AWS subscription revenue is contracted and rate-insensitive on a 12–24 month forward basis. At ~$175–$180 post-FOMC, AMZN trades at the lowest valuation relative to AWS revenue growth since the 2022 cloud deceleration. The BofA 3-hike framework (Sep/Oct/Dec 2026) creates a macro headwind that is specific to discretionary consumer (Prime retail) but not to AWS enterprise subscriptions — the split-thesis (AWS accumulation vehicle, not retail) is the right framework.
ideas.driver: AWS AI workload attach rates + Trainium/Inferentia inference cost advantage compounding toward cost parity with NVIDIA GPU workloads; Prime and logistics flywheel operational leverage at scale; Hormuz reopening reducing shipping cost inflation 5–10% (Amazon-specific logistics tailwind from Iran ceasefire); AI-native robotics expansion in fulfillment centers; Micron June 24 AWS AI capex validation; Project Kuiper satellite broadband competing with Starlink for enterprise connectivity.
ideas.risk: Cloud spending deceleration if BofA 3-hike 2026 forecast materializes into enterprise IT budget tightening — AWS is not immune to broad enterprise cost-cutting; competitive pressure from Azure and Google Cloud on enterprise AI workload share; Trainium/Inferentia ramp timelines extending beyond 2027 on yield issues; logistics cost inflation reversing Hormuz-reopening gains if Iran ceasefire fails.

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: LONG-TERM CONVICTION DOWNGRADED TO LOW on Day 2 stop execution — full exit gate triggered at $62,377 (Crypto.com live 11:07 UTC); two-consecutive-UTC-daily-close protocol executed; fixed-supply × ETF-access × halving thesis intact on 2–4 year horizon but requires re-entry confirmation after macro regime normalizes.
ideas.why: The Day 2 stop execution at $62,377 is a framework event, not a fundamental change in the long-term BTC thesis. The long-term structural drivers remain intact: fixed supply (21M BTC hard cap), widening institutional access (IBIT AUM compounding), April 2024 halving supply reduction, and DXY structural decline as Hormuz reopening removes oil-inflation anchor. However, the two-consecutive-close stop clock protocol (Day 1: June 23 UTC close below $63,500; Day 2: June 24 session $62,377 at 11:07 UTC, high $63,114 — $386 below threshold) has triggered the full exit gate — this is the protocol's designed response to a regime of sustained price below the structural support level. The downgrade from MEDIUM to LOW reflects: (1) full exit executed per framework; (2) re-entry requires new support confirmation at $60,000–$62,000 zone with two consecutive UTC closes above $62,000; (3) macro regime (VIX 19.49, DXY 101.38, BofA 3-hike) is structurally hostile to speculative assets on a 2–6 week horizon; (4) the $60,000–$62,000 re-entry zone is 0–3.7% below current price — it is not a deep value opportunity but a confirmation-based re-entry structure. The long-term 2–4 year thesis restarts after the macro regime normalizes (VIX below 17, SPX above 7,460, DXY below 100) and the $60,000–$62,000 support zone is confirmed with two consecutive UTC closes above $62,000.
ideas.driver: Fixed supply meeting widening institutional access (ETFs compounding AUM — IBIT, FBTC, ARKB combined AUM $28B+; corporate treasury adoption); DXY structural decline as Hormuz reopening removes the oil-inflation driver that anchored dollar strength in H1 2026; halving cycle supply reduction (April 2024) creating structural supply deficit that compounds over 3–5 years; 'digital gold' narrative in Warsh 'no forward guidance' regime creating non-correlated store-of-value demand; Lightning Network and Layer 2 adoption extending BTC utility beyond pure store-of-value.
ideas.risk: ★ Full exit executed June 24 per Day 2 stop clock — re-entry requires VIX below 17, SPX above 7,460, DXY below 100, AND two consecutive UTC closes above $62,000 in the $60,000–$62,000 zone; BofA 3-hike 2026 forecast materializing (Sep/Oct/Dec) creates sustained DXY above 103, structurally compressing speculative assets through Q4 2026; new $60,000–$62,000 support zone fails to hold after re-entry (structural decline to $55,000–$58,000 next major support); sustained IBIT outflows following double-bottom breach signal institutional de-risking at scale.
